memory_update.text: KRT is the cleanest underfollowed small-cap public candidate for restaurant foodservice disposables and eco-friendly packaging exposure; prioritize verification of chain/customer mix, eco-friendly sales mix durability, and margin sensitivity.
GPK is a direct public reference name for QSR cups, trays, and containers with named national restaurant customers, but it is broader paperboard packaging rather than a pure restaurant supplier.

SEE is a second-order restaurant packaging systems candidate through foodservice operators, QSR suppliers, and Liquibox/CRYOVAC applications; exposure is less visible and requires segment/end-market verification.

Pactiv Evergreen would have been highly relevant to the node but is no longer US-listed after the Novolex acquisition and Nasdaq delisting on April 1, 2025; use only as private-company competitive context.

Several strong sustainable foodservice packaging brands found in search, including World Centric, Vegware, Tellus, and Dart/Solo, are private or not clean US-listed candidates; they should be used as competitive and customer-channel context rather than candidate tickers.

KRT should be the primary underfollowed public candidate for restaurant takeout/delivery/sustainable packaging because it is small-cap, directly tied to disposable foodservice products, and has compostable Karat Earth exposure.
GPK should be retained as a reference/comparable for scaled QSR paperboard foodservice packaging, with explicit cups/lids/containers and named QSR customer evidence.
AMCR is a large-cap reference after the Berry Global combination; restaurant exposure is plausible through Berry foodservice products but diluted by Amcor's broader global packaging platform.

REYN remains a speculative shadow candidate until B2B restaurant or distributor channel exposure is verified; current evidence supports food-contact and compostable tableware adjacency but not direct restaurant dependency.

Several highly relevant foodservice packaging assets appear private or no longer separately public, including Novolex/Pactiv Evergreen and Footprint; later layers should map these as private competitors/customers/benchmarks rather than stock candidates.

KRT is the highest-priority underfollowed public candidate for the takeout/delivery/coffee/sustainable packaging node because it is a small-cap direct foodservice disposables supplier with eco-friendly product lines.

CLW should remain in the speculative shadow lane as an upstream paperboard/cupstock input candidate; it is below the preferred USD 300M market-cap cutoff and needs converter/customer linkage verification.

GPK provides a useful public reference benchmark for QSR packaging exposure because filings explicitly mention cups, lids, food containers, foodservice companies, QSRs, and named restaurant customers.

Regulatory/testing/certification gates may be a separate sub-node: ULS, SGS, Intertek, and Bureau Veritas-type TIC providers can matter if food-contact, PFAS, compostability, recyclability, or sustainability claims become mandatory customer requirements, but financial materiality to restaurant packaging remains unverified.

Pactiv Evergreen would have been an obvious reference foodservice packaging asset, but it appears no longer US-listed after Novolex's 2025 acquisition, so comparable work should focus on GPK, KRT, CLW, and private-company context such as Novolex/Dart only as anchors.

KRT is the highest-priority underfollowed small-cap candidate for the restaurant packaging node because it directly maps to foodservice disposables, cups, lids, containers, compostable products, restaurant chains, and distribution.

GPK should remain in the universe as a mid-cap paperboard/QSR foodservice packaging candidate, but later layers must quantify how material cups, lids, and food containers are to total revenue and margins.

Several pure-play foodservice packaging leaders are private or no longer independently listed, including Dart Container, Novolex, Pactiv Evergreen, and Eco-Products; this creates a public-market mapping gap that may make smaller listed suppliers more interesting but also harder to validate.

The key chokepoint variables for this node are not only demand volume but certified compostable/recyclable materials, food-contact compliance, chain-level reliability, printing/branding capability, distribution reach, and cost pass-through under resin, paperboard, freight, and tariff volatility.

node: Takeout, delivery, coffee cup, cold beverage, and sustainable packaging
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded the direct public-company universe for restaurant takeout, delivery, cups, cold beverage, and sustainable packaging. The cleanest underfollowed public exposure found in this pass is Karat Packaging, a small-cap disposable foodservice packaging supplier with meaningful restaurant/foodservice use and an eco-friendly product line. Graphic Packaging is a mid-cap reference/direct leader with explicit quick-service restaurant customers and cups, trays, and containers exposure. Sealed Air is a mid-cap second-order packaging platform for foodservice operators and QSR suppliers, especially sauces, condiments, proteins, dairy, liquid egg, and bag-in-box systems rather than consumer-facing takeout containers. Amcor is a large-cap reference after the Berry Global acquisition, relevant for scale and foodservice packaging but less pure and likely more followed. Pactiv Evergreen was excluded from candidates because it was acquired by Novolex and delisted from Nasdaq on April 1, 2025. Layer 1B expands the restaurant packaging/regulatory node into a two-lane public-market universe. The strongest underfollowed direct exposure found is Karat Packaging, a small-cap manufacturer/distributor of disposable and compostable foodservice products. Graphic Packaging is a more established reference/quality-comparable name with explicit QSR customer exposure in cups, lids, and food containers. Amcor is a larger reference name after absorbing Berry Global, which had direct foodservice cups/lids exposure, but its restaurant exposure is diluted inside a global packaging platform.
